Blaine leaders try to balance keeping taxes down amid rising population

Instaread
Harrison Klopp KSTP
Updated: August 10, 2026 - 8:53 PM
Published: August 10, 2026 - 7:50 PM

Blaine’s growing pains, city debates property tax increase

Blaine leaders are weighing a property tax increase as the fast-growing suburb says it needs more money to keep up with growth.

The Blaine City Council has a Monday evening meeting where they will discuss a potential 8.9% tax increase. Mayor Tim Sanders told 5 EYEWITNESS NEWS the increase is tied to inflation, public safety and infrastructure for a growing population.

“Blaine is a very hot market and has been with a lot of new constructions going on there. They’re building quite a few homes. They are one of the top 4 markets in the Twin Cities area,” said Joel Friday, a realtor with Keller Williams Classic.

He said Blaine draws people for youth sports, golf, open land and affordability.

The city is now considering what could amount to a tax increase of 8.9% for residents.

“We knew we had to grow up as a city,” said Sanders. “We were kind of that small, medium-sized city and becoming one of the top 10 cities in the state of Minnesota as far as population and all that, we knew we had to transition how we did things.”

Sanders said rising costs have played a role in recent levy increases, but infrastructure costs and how the city pays for them have been the biggest factor in higher property taxes. Sanders explained that the city focused on cash payments a few years ago to avoid having to borrow money in future years.

“Yeah, it’s a great question, and I would say we do realize and we do understand our property taxpayers. We do, it’s not just the cost of government, the cost of life right now is so expensive and just the cost of living nowadays has gone up so much. We understand that,” said Sanders. “That’s why we’re working on bringing those costs down over time.”

Blaine’s official tax levy increase is not expected to be voted on until December. If approved at the current level, it would add $120 a year for the average household in Blaine.
